title: Melancholic short-film underscore with rain
prompt: Output: one WAV, 48 kHz / 16-bit / stereo, exactly 2,880,000 samples (60.0 s at 30 fps = 1800 frames). Python + numpy/scipy only. Synthesise everything (no samples, no downloads, no speech). Fixed random seed (np.random.default_rng(55)). A 60-second melancholic animated-short underscore in D major at 74 BPM (1 beat = 24.32 frames). Frames 0-150: a hazy wide pad (D, A, F#, slow chorus) and distant city air noise. Frames 150-750: a music-box line (sine partials 1, 2.76, 5.4 with 1.5 s decay, slight mechanical timing jitter ±8 ms) plays an original, slow, mostly stepwise melody over Dmaj7 → Bm7 → Gmaj9 → A6, with a soft sine bass on roots; light warm 'play' textures: occasional soft wood knocks. Frames 750-840: thinning, pad only, energy drops 12 dB. Frame 840: a filtered pink-noise rain bed fades in (high-passed 1 kHz, wide stereo, random droplet ticks 2-6 kHz at ~25/s) and stays until frame 1170; harmony turns to Bm(add9) → Gmaj7 with low cello-like saw (1.2 kHz low-pass) swells; a lone music-box note every 2 bars, slightly detuned. Frame 1170: rain gutters out over 30 frames, a single low D2 cello note and a final music-box D6 on frame 1260, ring to silence by frame 1800 (last 10 s are a long, quiet decay of pad and air). Stereo side/mid ~0.6, nothing above -14 LUFS short-term at the climax. Master: -14 LUFS integrated, true peak <= -1 dBTP (4x oversampled peak check), last frames fade to exactly 0. You can't listen, so verify: measure loudness and true peak with ffmpeg ebur128 (peak=true), check the exact sample count, confirm the energy change lands on each cue frame, check every note fits the chord under it, render a spectrogram PNG and inspect it. Fix and re-render until every check passes, then report the numbers.
notes: 60 s melancholic D-major underscore: hazy pad, music-box melody, thinning drop, then filtered rain bed and quiet cello/music-box close.
